payload.claim: Every test that exercises `_since_newest_task` (`test_the_default_view_starts_at_the_newest_task`, `test_the_whole_log_is_still_reachable_behind_a_flag`) drives `follow` with the `_once` poll, so `follow` only ever executes a single iteration of its `while True` loop — `first_poll` is always `True` on the one and only poll these tests run. Nothing in the suite exercises a `Ceilings` event arriving in a *later* poll's batch (e.g. the tail of an old task plus a new task's `Ceilings` and its lines all appended together while the follower was asleep), which is exactly the scenario the docstring at lines 195-204 claims to handle correctly ('a `Ceilings` a spec driven again writes while this follower is already running arrives on a later poll like anything else appended since the poll before it, and following continues past it rather than clearing the screen'). Changing line 213 from `if first_poll and not whole_log:` to `if not whole_log:` makes the cut apply on every poll, not just the first — so if a later poll's batch happens to contain a task boundary, everything before that boundary in that batch (e.g. the previous task's own terminal/teardown lines that hadn't been flushed yet) would be silently dropped instead of rendered. Every existing test still passes after this edit, because none of them ever puts a `Ceilings` event into a non-first poll's batch.
